angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: mean acceleration over the 1.0 s around the sharpest point of the cut), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner), tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes. Last season's route-shrunk SOE is the positive use, as a day-3 tiebreaker with GO/HOLD calls for 2026.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 on unseen classes; best case +1.0 in = 0.14 catches a season. Baseline without tracking: held-out R2 0.00 [-0.51, 0.14], RMSE 8.6 in, rho 0.12; Break G delta R2 0.013 [-0.157, 0.085]. Same-route true correlation 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32], n=99, vs official 40 to full-play NFL top speed 0.43 [0.29, 0.54] within position (raw pooled 0.74). Day-3 tiebreaker gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], 20 pairs, rule closer on 12 of 20; earlier lists 7/13 (54% [32, 75]) vs base 8/20 (40%).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_16/revised applying all twelve top_changes. Football: one headline margin (upper 90% bound +1.0 in = 0.14 catches; the +/-3 TOST moved to an appendix note); shortlist leads with GO (Washington, Douglas: listed again after an earlier hit) and HOLD (Tez Johnson, Arian Smith: first listing) by a stated rule, man/zone splits replaced by a three-item film checklist, earlier lists vs base rate with Jeffreys intervals (7/13 54% [32,75] vs 8/20 40% [24,58]); all 20 day-3 pairs shown as a paired forecast-error contrast with WR (10/15) and TE (2/5) separate and a WR-only gain; 'what would change the call' with simulated 2026 power (0.27) and a negative-gain rate under a real edge (10%). Data science: speed benchmark recomputed on the full-play window and stated (0.43 within position/year, 0.74 raw pooled WR+TE matching the judge, 0.34 restricted snap-to-throw window), all in numbers.json; baseline held-out R2/RMSE/rank correlation and Break G delta R2 with class-stratified intervals; P tempered with the top-bin calibration (14/23, 61%) and 'read P as an ordering'; simulated power of the pre-registered 2026 test. Writeup: lede defines Break G and SOE first then a ~50-word result; motivation split in two and explains the last receiver spot and the $1.08M; machinery (72% within +/-0.2, split-half -0.06, shuffle p, one-sided p) moved to the appendix; action 1 now 'only ties' with the coin-flip rationale; action 3 split into a finding and a labelled film hypothesis; history table folded into the verdict table and Fig 4. Viz: Fig 1 = five receivers at Combine percentiles 5/25/50/75/95 with league-median reference and bootstrap ribbons, headline numbers in the subtitle; Fig 2 = single full-width forest with pooled band, speed band, power<25% legend, 0.2 label moved, text >= 11 pt; Fig 4 = paired-contrast dot plot of all 20 pairs plus 2026 GO/HOLD mini-cards. check.py: 1,906 words, 4 figures + 3 tables.
open_risks: The day-3 edge is still not proven: the season-fold interval includes 0, draft-class folds halve the gain (0.15), and the rule barely beats raw last-season SOE (0.09 [-0.19, 0.40]).
The judges cited '24 matched pairs'; the analysis has 20 day-3 season pairs with outcomes (the 24 are 2025 matched pairs with no outcome yet). All 20 are shown, not 24.
Delta R2 for Break G is slightly positive (0.013) because its slope is negative; the text says so, but a skim reader may misread it.
The 40-vs-top-speed benchmark depends on the scale: 0.43 within position and year (used, matches Break G's scale) vs 0.74 raw pooled; the judge's 0.74 is reported in the appendix.
GO/HOLD rule (listed again after an earlier hit) was set after seeing the history; the freeze date (24 October 2026) is after the 2026 season began and the 2026 test has simulated power 0.27.
